question: Should nix-openclaw add a supported Gmail-hook golden-path example/interface now, or rely on the upstream documented `hooks.gmail` contract until the pull-model design is settled?
rationale: The immediate status-400 problem has a documented upstream configuration fix, while a Nix-specific first-class path changes the public consumer interface and needs a maintainer-owned scope decision.

options.title: Add a minimal README example
options.body: Document the existing upstream-safe `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey` and prefix configuration in `README.md` without adding new Nix module options.

options.title: Wait for the pull-model design
options.body: Keep the generic config passthrough as the supported path until the upstream pull model defines the stable Nix integration boundary.

recommendation.title: Add a minimal README example
recommendation.body: Document the existing upstream-safe `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey` and prefix configuration in `README.md` without adding new Nix module options.

likelyOwner.reason: They explicitly connected the requested Nix experience to the upstream pull-model work and have recent history maintaining this package surface.
